name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Pick over the rice and split moong dal, rinse together in several changes of water, and drain. Measure the remaining ingredients before heating the cooker.
Warm ghee in the pressure cooker over medium heat. Add cumin and let it sizzle briefly until fragrant, taking care not to darken it.
Add the drained rice and dal, turmeric, salt and measured water. Stir once to loosen anything on the base, then close the cooker without exceeding its marked fill limit for grains and pulses.
Cook according to the cooker instructions for about 8–10 minutes at pressure. Let the pressure release naturally and open only when the cooker indicates it is safe.
Stir firmly enough to bring the rice and dal together. Both should be completely soft, with no firm centre; if needed, add hot water and continue cooking until tender.
For a spoonable khichdi, add hot water in small splashes and simmer briefly. It thickens as it stands, so finish slightly looser than you want to serve it.
tips: A soft texture is intended. Do not fill a pressure cooker beyond its manufacturer’s limit.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
